newsitem.title: USA: Consumer confidence edged lower but still strong.
newsitem.headline: Consumer confidence edged lower but still strong.

text.p: Consumer confidence edged lower but remained strong in February, the Conference Board said Tuesday, the latest sign pointing to continued moderate economic growth.
The New York-based business research group said its Consumer Confidence Index stood at 118.4, barely lower than January's strong revised reading of 118.7.

"Consumer confidence held steady in February largely because consumers continue to view current business activity as strong," said Lynn Franco, Associate Director of the group's Consumer Research Centre.

The group said its reading on consumers' "present situation" jumped more than two points in February to the highest level in 27 years. Consumers' expectations for business conditions over the next months edged lower, it said.
Consumers account for about two-thirds of the economy through their purchases of goods and services, so readings of consumer sentiment are watched closely by policy-makers and in financial markets.

Economists had predicted a slight drop in confidence in February. But the February reading and January's revised figure came in stronger than economists' forecasts for 116.1 in February vs. the 116.8 originally reported for January.
The board revised the January reading based on late data that was "more upbeat," Franco said.
Consumers were slightly more upbeat about the job market in February, with 32 percent saying jobs were plentiful, up from just under 31 percent in January, the group said.
The survey is based on a sample of 5,000 households and is conducted for the Conference Board by NFO Research Inc., a research firm in Greenwich, Conn.
